summary: The render foundation: Forward+ on the desktop with gl_compatibility declared as the mobile fallback, a RenderProfile autoload that names the features the live method cannot do, one island WorldEnvironment resource and scene, a fixed isometric camera director, and a seven-shader material library the two procedural setpieces adopt in place of their flat StandardMaterial3D colours.

coordination.notes: Branched from origin/backend/b0-expedition-state at f5d26d1; merged trunk mid-lane at bea81f0 to pick up P1. game/project.godot is touched in three places only: the [rendering] block, one autoload appended at the END of [autoload], and a new [shader_globals] section appended at the end of the file (the global wind, wind_heading and motion_scale the foliage and water shaders read; nothing else in the repository declares shader globals, so the section is new rather than shared). AGENTS.md section 0, three times. (1) My lane had extended game/tools/capture_review_scene.gd to take a scene list in one engine process; P1 landed the same idea, better, in the same file. The merge conflict was resolved as P1's file whole and nothing of the P2 extension survives beside it. (2) game/scripts/review/elizabethan_port_town_review.gd existed only to look_at a camera. The camera rig now owns framing declaratively through its frame_target export, so that script is DELETED rather than left duplicating the rig; the scene keeps its review-purpose metadata. (3) The reception terrace lighting kit and the port town set each built their own Environment and their own sun. Both now instance res://render/world_environment.tscn and set only the hour and the weather through its exported properties -- one light rig, two settings, and the same seam P3 drives. Two edits fall outside the card's literal file list and are named here rather than hidden: the port town set's Environment section gained a HarborBed and HarborShelf (a depth-shaded sea needs a bottom before it can be shallow; without one the whole harbour rendered as the open-ocean tone), and the terrace review scene gained a shore, a sloped beach and a sea plane, each marked in its own metadata as review staging that is not part of the world cell. No world-cell geometry, collision, navigation, anchor or ID was touched. Two library materials have no caller yet and are not pretending otherwise: stylised_river.tres (P4's board water, or a river when one is authored) and placeholder.tres (whatever is next to lose its art direction). Both are named deliverables of this card and both are held by the suite.
